api-errors.reason: ThalovantApiError in src/errors.ts carries statusCode, code, detail and a non-enumerable problem, filled by apiError() in src/control.ts for every failed control-plane response, device-flow polling included; the message is unchanged. Run against the shared api-error vectors, each served by a loopback node:http peer and read back through getHub(), plus a device sign-in poll and a createClientIdentity() whose generated secrets stay redacted. Secrets the SDK sent are scrubbed from the body before it is parsed in every spelling a JSON body gives them (as sent, JSON-escaped, and with non-ASCII \u-escaped in either case, src/redact.ts), and a device-token refusal scrubs the device code the same way; an echoed validation input is never repeated in a message, whatever its key. It also carries fields, the setting or secret names a refusal lists in the problem's fields at its top or inside an object detail (strings only, never values, empty when absent), which the error's JSON shows beside statusCode and detail. Since 0.11.0 a JSON body is scrubbed once parsed rather than in its text (redactSecretsInJson in src/redact.ts): every decoded string and key, and a number that spells a secret, so no JSON spelling can decode a secret back into problem or the message and no escape is cut in two; a body that is not JSON keeps the text pass. A secret under 8 characters is replaced only where it stands alone (no letter or digit beside it). A number in a JSON body that spells a secret is replaced in the text before parsing can round it (redactSecretsInJsonNumbers), overlapping occurrences of secrets are replaced together, and a parsed body nested deeper than 64 levels is cut there, so that neither the scrub nor JSON.stringify overflows before the error carrying its status is made. A text body is scrubbed in one pass over every secret and every JSON spelling of it, and markers are found by binary search, so a body full of them stays near-linear.

binary.reason: decodeHiveBinaryFrame branches on BINARY: four bits of payload type, then the clip itself, never parsed or inflated. onBinary() delivers it. A compressed part of any other frame -- its metadata or JSON payload -- inflates to at most 32 MiB (MAX_INFLATED_BYTES, zlib's maxOutputLength in src/platform/node.ts), and one that would inflate further, or is truncated, is refused; browsers refuse compressed parts outright. Run against the shared binary vectors and against binary-frames.json, which is hivemind-bus-client's own encoder output rather than a frame this SDK built for itself, and test/wire-limits.test.ts for the inflation cap.

the browser map swaps in src/loopback.browser.ts, which refuses) before building the URL with browserAuthorizationUrl() (the contract's order, RFC 3986 encoding, scope left out when empty, device_name cut to 120 code points and left out when empty; only a missing deviceName gets the default) and loopbackRedirectUri(), prints the URL or hands it to prompt, opens it without waiting, and waits on the monotonic clock, never early. classifyRequest() serves only GET /callback (404 otherwise; a HEAD answer has no body), answers a missing, repeated or wrong state with a 400 (timingSafeEqual on the UTF-8 bytes) and keeps waiting, decodes the query once as a form does, lets any error win over a code and keeps only RFC 6749's seven error codes; the first accepted callback stops the listening, a second on an open connection is a 400, the accepted tab gets its page with the five page headers once the sign-in has ended, however long that takes, and every answered connection is shut for writing and drained for at most 2 s and 1 MiB before it closes. send() refuses any request off the API's origin. After the second review: the 10-second bound holds even against a fetch that ignores its signal or a body that never ends; close() waits for the accepted connection's drain within its 1-second grace; a HEAD gets no body on a 400 either; an opener's rejection is always observed. After the third review: at the bound the body being read is cancelled through its reader; a prompt that cancels the sign-in opens nothing; a secret reaching into a marker takes the marker with it.

connection-admission.reason: waitForAdmission() follows the create's operation with GET /v1/operations/{id}, every read bounded by what is left of the wait: ready resolves, failed and timed_out reject with ThalovantAdmissionFailedError(errorCode, no status), 404 and no operation resolve at once, a 5xx is ridden out, and a 429 waits max(poll interval, the problem's retry_after_seconds, else Retry-After, else RateLimit-Reset), a timeout at once when that is more than is left. 401 and 403 pass through as the API's own error (ThalovantAuthError), an API out of reach as ThalovantApiUnreachableError, and any other refusal of the wait is ThalovantAdmissionFailedError keeping statusCode, code, detail and problem. The deadline rejects with ThalovantAdmissionTimeoutError (instanceof both ThalovantConnectionError and ThalovantTimeoutError), ending "it may still admit it later"; waits are re-armed on the monotonic clock. A links.self on another origin (scheme, host, port) is never fetched. Run against the shared admission vectors over a loopback node:http peer that sends the case's headers, with {api_host}/{api_port} filled in and a closed port for an unreachable API.

home-link.reason: src/home.ts answers each thalovant.home.request at most once, never after the hub's 10 s counted from its arrival: the handler gets its 9 s or what is left of the bound (Promise.race against a timer, so a handler that ignores its AbortSignal cannot hold the answer back), and the reply's sending gets what the handler left, withdrawn at the bound through a SendOptions signal that ThalovantClient.reply()/emit() and the transports' send chain honour before encrypting. The reply is built by replyContext() in src/events.ts from the context exactly as the hub sent it (a destination with no source gives no destination). Speech is made by stripSsml() in src/rich.ts (real tags, comments and processing instructions only, scanned in one pass), decodeReferences() (numeric references, the XML five and nbsp only) and a White_Space collapse. Keeping the link: closeRefuses() and LinkSupervisor in src/link-keeping.ts are the pure close rule and supervisor; src/transport-core.ts reads a 1000/1005/1008 close as a refusal during any step of the handshake or within 750 ms after it, unless a frame from the hub decrypted first (heardFromHub; a close is judged after the frames that came before it are read), reads a refusal as an XX handshake ends -- a close, or an HTTPS request answered 401/403 while the last handshake frames go out or right after -- as ThalovantClientKeyRejectedError (a ThalovantHubRefusedError naming the key folder and the other likely one), follows a refused KK attempt with one XX attempt at once in the same connect (WSS, HTTP and MQTT), classifies a Noise message that does not authenticate as ThalovantHubRefusedError and a pin mismatch (checked before message 3, and in pinHubKey) as ThalovantHubKeyChangedError; HubSession.run() in src/session.ts follows the supervisor and stops at once on a changed key or a rejected client key. A reply withdrawn while it waits behind another frame is never sent and leaves the link as it was (the queued cases, over a real link). Run against the shared home-link vectors (directly and end to end over a real WSS + Noise link) and the link-keeping vectors: the pure rule, a loopback hub that records the patterns it sees and pins the client's key as hivemind-core does (connects made as a kept link makes them, the settle window included), and the supervisor.

runtime.reason: Applicable public behavior is implemented and exercised by the named regression suites and shared fixtures. HiveMind #251/#252 only changes the Python upstream client dispatcher; this consumer uses native single-dispatch transports (MCP delegates to the Node SDK), or caller-owned frame parsing in embedded C. No Python HiveMind bus dependency or slave-protocol reinjection exists here. Python now requires fixed upstream 1.1.9a1 and removes its identity-based suppression; equal independent native frames remain distinct. Reply claim metadata follows the Python string-ID contract, with first-seen ordering, case-sensitive fallback stages and legacy unstamped success. Invalid non-string stamps are ignored. Embedded C exposes bounded extraction and claim classification while its caller retains ordered IDs. A skill's own speak event may now assert `data.meta.thalovant_claimed === true` to positively claim a fallback-tier reply; `replyClaimMetadata` checks that first, only after the handled/ok/no-failure gate, so it can only turn a would-be false into true and a reply whose skill never sets it is judged exactly as before. The assertion scan is restricted to the skill's own `speak`/`ovos.utterance.speak` event (never the wider media-events set, and never another correlated event such as `ovos.utterance.handled` that this reply happens to carry with the same meta shape).
